steps.what: Review planetarium bookings, staff availability and equipment status
Set planetarium operating priorities and resolve resource conflicts
Write the operating schedule and staff assignments used by the team
Communicate the operating schedule and assignments to planetarium colleagues
Direct daily operations and respond to staffing, technical and visitor issues

tasks.design: Configure native booking and schedule views in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {CALENDAR}, then reuse existing programme and assignment fields when writing the operating schedule. The astronomer retains priorities, staffing choices, team communication and operational judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated booking lookup and schedule headings can accompany operational direction.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking and calendar fields can support a consolidated view and reusable schedule structure.
tasks.still_hard: Staff, equipment and visitor needs can conflict and change during operations.
tasks.human_edge: Balance scientific quality, practical resources and the visitor experience.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time rebuilding schedules and more time resolving operational issues.

reach.learn: Keep operational assignments linked to current bookings and equipment availability.

evidence.claim: Native booking views and reusable schedule fields could reduce repeated administrative work; planetarium decisions and the proposed time saving are unmeasured.

assumptions: The boundary includes the current schedule and assignments actually used by staff and their separate communication. No new daily activity report or trailing log is added.

Booking staff maintain session identifiers, times and group requirements. Staff or roster owners provide current availability, and technical staff provide dated equipment status during existing work. S1 includes retrieval and reconciliation; missing or stale information requires direct clarification rather than an inferred available flag.

The astronomer makes resource decisions in s2 and captures the actual assignments in retained s3 time. The view removes 3 hours of navigation; schedule defaults remove 6 hours of repeated session headings and identifiers while retaining conflict resolution and individual assignments.
Try native scheduling features before custom code. No automatic staff allocation, visitor messaging or equipment control is proposed. Ordinary author saves remain retained without self-approval.
unknowns: Whether the astronomer currently writes the operating schedule.
Whether booking and roster fields are already shared.
research_questions: Observe a current scheduling cycle and measure lookup and repeated entry separately from staffing decisions and operational response.

incremental.description: Maintain schedule defaults and operational view references

approvals.approved_version: Exact operating schedule, session dates, staff assignments and colleague recipients; changed schedules require checking again before communication.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=91, gross 9 minus 2 upkeep gives central net 7. Conservative case: incompatible booking/status sources retain 14/15 lookup hours and bespoke sessions retain 19/20 schedule hours plus 65 fixed: 98 retained, 2 gross minus 2 =0. Compatible booking and programme fields retain 13 lookup and 16 schedule hours plus 65 fixed: 94 retained, 6 gross minus 2 =4. Existing automated schedules supply no eligible repeated entry benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep scientific and operational direction with the astronomer while reducing repeated scheduling administration.
reach: Compare public programme coordination with museum operations staff.
role.ambitious_version: A planetarium directed through current, usable schedules and accountable daily judgement.
